entries.problem: A joining line or visual decoration changes the stored Arabic component.
entries.safeguard: Keep canonical sourceText separate from displayText and reconstruct only from sourceText.

entries.problem: Only a prefix or partial component is shown for a complete word.
entries.safeguard: Validate that ordered parts reconstruct the complete visible occurrence; use truthful atomic mode when a reviewed split is unavailable.

entries.problem: A repeated word inherits an unrelated occurrence explanation.
entries.safeguard: Reuse shared lexical data only where appropriate and retain occurrence-specific grammar, meaning and overrides.

entries.problem: Labels such as Whole word or Main word are mistaken for reviewed analysis.
entries.safeguard: Reject placeholder labels for custom-complete content and block publication until reviewed data exists.

entries.problem: Multiple workers edit the same sūrah package or canonical database rows.
entries.safeguard: Workers write unique immutable packet revisions; one deterministic assembler and serialized importer own canonical writes.

entries.problem: A structural Ṣarf pass labels a family limited because it found too few Qur'anic candidates, because authoring effort was missing, or because an outer compound label contains a preposition. This wrongly treats a rootful lexical noun, verb or adjective as a restricted grammatical item.
entries.safeguard: Treat every existing limited family as pending independent linguistic audit. Separate rootless grammatical components from rootful lexical stems, inspect canonical forms and approved linguistic evidence, and either author exactly five useful reviewed forms or record a specific confirmed-limited/blocked decision. Never use provider candidate count, an outer preposition label, missing authoring effort or boilerplate as a linguistic limitation reason.

entries.problem: The same generic limitedReason is copied onto unrelated particles, proper nouns and lexical families, so the record does not explain why this particular family is limited.
entries.safeguard: Require a lexeme- and category-specific reason that names the actual grammatical or lexical restriction, the genuine forms reviewed, the missing useful contrast and the evidence checked.

entries.problem: A limited family passes structural validation without a current human-quality linguistic decision, leaving the old classification unchallenged.
entries.safeguard: Every limited occurrence must carry a current audit decision: confirmed-limited, upgraded-to-full or blocked-for-genuine-ambiguity. Unknown and pending are not complete; blocked families cannot be custom-complete.

entries.problem: A lesson's Ṣarf / form-family section contains too few useful reviewed forms, so the learner cannot compare the pattern and morphological changes.
entries.safeguard: The normal target is exactly five distinct reviewed forms: the current Qur'anic form first plus four useful related forms. Accuracy outranks row count; use a specific reviewed limited family only when five would require fabrication, duplication, irrelevant forms, misleading morphology or weak padding.

entries.problem: A generic authoring fallback manufactures Ṣarf rows from the current word, bare root letters, a provider lemma or grammatical case endings.
entries.safeguard: Automatically generated forms are candidates only. Every approved row needs a real appropriately vocalised Arabic form, form-specific English meaning, meaningful distinction, root/lexeme relationship and provenance. If reliable evidence remains conflicting, block rather than guess.

entries.problem: A reviewer treats the Ṣarf section as a list of near-synonyms, rejects genuine same-root derived forms because their meanings differ, or mistranslates every form as though it had the Qur'anic occurrence's meaning. This hides how Arabic roots develop across derived forms and across nouns, adjectives and participles.
entries.safeguard: Use same root as the primary organising principle. Accept genuinely attested, morphologically useful forms even when the semantic branch develops, but translate each form according to its own meaning and explain the relationship explicitly. Reject only wrong-root, weakly attested, shell-only, duplicate or pedagogically empty rows.

entries.problem: A C1 adjudication copies rows from any previously full lesson sharing the root and then treats four copied rows as proof of a full family. This can mix derived branches incorrectly, preserve spelling errors, or accept an imperative with a conjunction removed as a new row.
entries.safeguard: C1 and later adjudications must use an explicit reviewed family specification or an independently evidenced candidate record. Verify root ownership, form/pattern, vocalisation, form-specific meaning, semantic development, shell exclusion and pedagogical value for every row before approval. A row count is never evidence of linguistic correctness.

entries.problem: A compound surface word contains a lexical stem plus a grammatical part, but the whole lesson is marked rootless because the grammatical part has no root.
entries.safeguard: Keep the lexical stem/root as the lesson root and explain each attached grammatical part separately as No lexical root (category).

entries.problem: The Root Picture card repeats Arabic root letters or a rootless marker instead of teaching an English root meaning.
entries.safeguard: Keep root radicals and rootPicture separate. Lexical rootPicture must be an English semantic range; rootless rootPicture must begin with one category-specific No lexical root marker.

entries.problem: The current occurrence gloss is copied into Root Picture as if it were the stable root meaning.
entries.safeguard: Use content-import/root-meanings.json or an approved lexicon, and author a concise accurate semantic range when missing. Never derive rootPicture from the occurrence translation.

entries.problem: An explanatory paraphrase appears beneath the complete Arabic āyah instead of the certified direct translation.
entries.safeguard: Render the approved certified direct translation as the primary translation; keep naturalMeaning explanatory only and verify representative routes after import.

entries.problem: The basmalah is accidentally retained in the visible first āyah, shifting words and invalidating the translation relationship.
entries.safeguard: Preserve it only in sourceRawArabic where appropriate, remove it from visible āyah data for sūrahs other than 1 and 9, and validate the first visible word positions.

entries.problem: يَا is shortened to O rather than preserving the approved learner wording Oh.
entries.safeguard: Use Oh consistently in the gloss, lesson, form row, sentence role, recognition clue and takeaway, and validate the wording.

entries.problem: Provider morphology is attached by position even though its segments do not reconstruct the canonical occurrence.
entries.safeguard: Reconstruct and compare exact sourceText before using provider root, lemma or segmentation; quarantine failed alignments.

entries.problem: A missing provider root is treated as proof that a lexical content word is rootless.
entries.safeguard: Treat provider-root absence as a review state. Use No lexical root only for a reviewed grammatical/rootless component or a genuinely rootless item.

entries.problem: A morphology provider supplies a root for a grammatical or otherwise explicitly rootless occurrence, and the importer rejects the reviewed rootless teaching decision as a root mismatch.
entries.safeguard: Treat provider roots as evidence, not an automatic teaching answer. When the lesson has been explicitly reviewed as rootless and every breakdown component is marked rootless with a category-specific explanation, allow the provider root to remain evidence without promoting it to a lexical lesson root. Fail closed when the rootless decision is not explicit or any lexical component is present.

entries.problem: A root, provider lemma and part-of-speech key can merge a proper name, a common noun or a distinct lexical sense with a related derived family. One occurrence then receives a full family that is linguistically valid for a different sense, while other occurrences remain limited or blocked.
entries.safeguard: Review every mixed full/limited/blocked family occurrence by occurrence. Distinguish the actual lexeme and sense from the shared root, and record a stable reviewed familyScope when the same provider identity contains separate proper-name, common-lexeme or model families. Keep the current Qur'anic form first, propagate only a validated five-form family within the same scope, revoke defective full decisions, and keep unresolved scope conflicts blocked with a durable review record. Never treat a shared root or provider lemma alone as proof that forms belong in one learner family.
entries.evidence: Mixed-family reconciliation report, familyScope metadata, occurrence-level before/after ledger records and final family audit.

entries.problem: A provider assigns a lexical root that conflicts with the reviewed Arabic root family, often because a rare or quadriliteral form is conflated with a visually similar root. Blind provider agreement would preserve the wrong root and teach unrelated Ṣarf forms.
entries.safeguard: Treat provider roots as evidence rather than an automatic answer. When Codex independently establishes a different root from canonical Arabic, approved lexicons and the form's morphology, record an explicit reviewed root override with the provider root, reviewed root, rationale and provenance. Import and audit may accept the mismatch only when that override is present; every other lexical mismatch fails closed.

entries.problem: A structurally valid Ṣarf row belongs to a different Arabic root family than the lesson, so a wrong-root form can be taught as a related form.
entries.safeguard: Check every retained row's Arabic form, meaning and provenance against the lesson root and lexeme. Reject wrong-root rows even when they share a surface pattern; require approved lexicon, canonical evidence or explicit Codex linguistic provenance for every retained row.

entries.problem: A morphologically similar form from a neighbouring root family is copied into the current Ṣarf family, such as the ه د م passive participle مَهْدُومٌ being assigned to ه د د.
entries.safeguard: Before approving every Ṣarf row, independently verify the Arabic root radicals, vocalised pattern, lemma and meaning. Compare doubled-root and neighbouring-root forms explicitly, reject any row whose root ownership differs, and run a corpus-wide wrong-root search after every adjudication batch.

entries.problem: One lexical family is split into separate learner families because a second Qur’anic occurrence adds a grammatical shell such as ال, و, ف, a pronoun or a case ending, leaving equivalent occurrences with inconsistent Ṣarf rows.
entries.safeguard: After approving a family, locate every occurrence with the same reviewed root and lexical lemma even when its surface shell differs. Keep that occurrence’s complete Qur’anic form first, then propagate the approved family rows and provenance; never count the shell as an additional Ṣarf form.

entries.problem: A conjunction clitic such as وَ or فَ is counted as a new Ṣarf family form when it merely attaches to an otherwise unchanged lexical stem.
entries.safeguard: Separate conjunction clitics from lexical morphology. Do not count a canonical occurrence whose provider lexical stem is unchanged and whose only added material is وَ or فَ; explain the clitic in the word breakdown instead.

entries.problem: A deduplication key removes every final Arabic diacritic and collapses genuinely different lexical forms that share an unvocalised skeleton, such as حَضَّ (perfect verb) and حَضٌّ (verbal noun).
entries.safeguard: For duplicate detection, remove only terminal tanwin/case markers when they are the sole inflectional distinction. Preserve lexical vowels, shaddah and morphological pattern markers; use a part-of-speech-aware key so a final verb/verbal-noun vowel cannot be collapsed into a noun's case ending; require separate reviewed rows when the vocalised forms, meanings or morphological roles differ.

entries.problem: A verb such as نَفَرَ can be incorrectly treated as the same form as a noun such as نَفَرٌ when the audit strips the final vowel before comparing candidates, causing a genuine lexical contrast to disappear and leaving a family blocked.
entries.safeguard: Make Ṣarf candidate deduplication and current-form comparison part-of-speech-aware. Preserve the final lexical vowel for reviewed verb and verbal-noun candidates; strip terminal case/tanwin only for forms where it is genuinely inflectional. Add a regression case whenever a verb/noun pair shares an unvocalised skeleton.

entries.problem: Different candidate sources can retain the same lexical form with different case endings, causing the assembled Ṣarf family to contain duplicate rows and fail validation or falsely consume one of the four related-form slots.
entries.safeguard: After merging provider, existing-reviewed and Codex-authored candidates, deduplicate by the reviewed part-of-speech-aware inflectional key before selecting rows and again after assembly. Treat case-only and tanwin-only variants as one form; if deduplication leaves fewer than five meaningful rows, author or select another genuinely distinct reviewed form rather than padding.

entries.problem: Article, conjunction and case-only variants of the same lexical surface are counted as separate Ṣarf rows, allowing a family such as فُلْك to appear to have five forms without teaching five real lexical or morphological contrasts.
entries.safeguard: For Ṣarf family review, preserve the original fully vocalised Arabic rows but deduplicate article/conjunction shells and noun case endings for row-count purposes. Require each approved row to add a real lexical or morphological distinction; shell-only variants cannot satisfy the five-form target.

entries.problem: A fixed locative adverb such as حَيْثُ is copied from provider noun/root metadata and taught as a lexical root family, even though it has no productive lexical root for the learner to expand.
entries.safeguard: Review fixed locative adverbs independently of provider labels. When the Arabic item is genuinely indeclinable and rootless, set the lesson root to empty, use No lexical root (locative adverb), mark the breakdown component rootless, and keep its fixed form as a confirmed-limited grammatical lesson. Never invent ح ي ث Ṣarf rows merely because a provider emitted a root-like label.

entries.problem: Canonical API Arabic can include verse-stop symbols and invisible bidirectional control marks that are not present in the stored source word, causing a valid word to fail source/API alignment.
entries.safeguard: Normalize only decorative Qur'anic marks and Unicode bidirectional controls for alignment while preserving the original sourceText and API text for display/provenance. Fail closed for any remaining substantive mismatch, and add a regression case whenever a new provider mark appears.
